questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the AI Impact Summit 2026 held in New Delhi:
1. It was the first global AI summit hosted in the Global South.
2. The first of the annual summits was held at Bletchley Park, United Kingdom, in 2023.
3. The 2025 AI Action Summit was held in Seoul.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The New Delhi summit was the first of its kind hosted in the Global South, following Bletchley Park (2023), Seoul (2024) and Paris (2025). The 2025 AI Action Summit was in Paris, not Seoul. The summit was organised around 7 Chakras (working groups) and 3 Sutras (core principles).

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs about the M.A.N.A.V. framework for human-centric AI highlighted at the AI Impact Summit:
1. M : Moral and Ethical system
2. A : Accountable Governance
3. N : National Sovereignty
4. V : Verified and Voluntary
How many of the above pairs are correct?
questions.e: In the M.A.N.A.V. framework, M stands for Moral and Ethical system, A for Accountable Governance, N for National Sovereignty, the second A for Accessible and Inclusive AI and V for Valid and Legitimate. 'Verified and Voluntary' is not the expansion of V.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the models unveiled at the India AI Impact Summit 2026:
1. Sarvam AI unveiled open-source mixture-of-experts models Sarvam-30B and Sarvam-105B for 22 Indian languages.
2. The Sarvam models were trained on GPUs from the IndiaAI Mission's compute pool.
3. Param2, a 17-billion-parameter multilingual model, was launched by Sarvam AI.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Sarvam-30B and Sarvam-105B are open-source mixture-of-experts models for 22 Indian languages trained on IndiaAI Mission compute. Param2, a 17-billion-parameter multilingual model, was launched separately by BharatGen, not by Sarvam AI.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the IndiaAI Mission's compute capacity announced in February 2026:
1. India announced 20,000 more GPUs for the compute pool, which had about 38,000 GPUs.
2. The target is over 100,000 GPUs by the end of 2026.
3. The IndiaAI Mission is implemented by NITI Aayog.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: India announced 20,000 more GPUs on top of about 38,000, targeting over 100,000 by the end of 2026. The IndiaAI Mission is implemented by the IndiaAI independent business division under MeitY, not by NITI Aayog. Its outlay is Rs 10,372 crore, approved in March 2024.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about SAHI and BODH launched by the Union Health Minister in February 2026:
1. SAHI is the Strategy for Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare for India, a guidance framework for safe and ethical health AI.
2. BODH was developed by IIT Kanpur with the National Health Authority.
3. BODH requires the underlying health datasets to be shared with the evaluators.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: SAHI is the national framework for safe and ethical health AI and BODH is the Benchmarking Open Data Platform for Health AI built by IIT Kanpur with the NHA. BODH evaluates models on real-world health data without sharing the underlying datasets.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about VoicERA, unveiled at the India AI Impact Summit 2026:
1. It is an open-source end-to-end voice AI stack built on the BHASHINI National Language Infrastructure.
2. BHASHINI is an AI-powered language translation platform under the National Language Translation Mission.
3. VoicERA is a closed proprietary stack owned by a private company.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: MeitY unveiled VoicERA as an open-source voice AI stack on BHASHINI, the AI translation platform run by the Digital India BHASHINI Division of the Digital India Corporation. It is not a closed proprietary stack.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the initiatives announced under the New Delhi Declaration at the India AI Impact Summit 2026:
1. The Global AI Impact Commons is a shared platform of AI use cases that countries can scale and replicate.
2. The Trusted AI Commons is a repository of tools, benchmarks and best practices for secure and trustworthy AI systems.
3. Both Commons create legally binding obligations on the countries that endorsed the Declaration.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Global AI Impact Commons spreads proven AI use cases, and the Trusted AI Commons collects tools, benchmarks and best practices for trustworthy AI. The Declaration is a non-binding political commitment, so neither Commons imposes legal obligations.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the CERT-In advisory framework for the space ecosystem released in February 2026:
1. CERT-In and the Satcom Industry Association of India jointly released it.
2. CERT-In is designated as the national nodal agency under Section 70B of the Information Technology Act, 2000.
3. CERT-In functions under the Ministry of Home Affairs.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: CERT-In and SIA-India jointly released the framework for satellite operators, ground stations and vendors. CERT-In, the national nodal agency for computer security incidents under Section 70B of the IT Act, 2000, has worked under MeitY since 2004, not under the Home Ministry.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about India Semiconductor Mission (ISM) 2.0 announced in the Union Budget 2026-27:
1. It focuses on producing equipment and materials and designing full-stack Indian intellectual property.
2. It also targets industry-led research and training centres.
3. Rs 10,000 crore was allocated to it for FY2026-27.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: ISM 2.0 targets equipment and materials production, full-stack Indian IP and industry-led research and training centres. The allocation for FY2026-27 is Rs 1,000 crore, not Rs 10,000 crore. The Budget also stresses fabrication and packaging capacity.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Gaganyaan drogue parachute test of 18 February 2026:
1. It was a qualification-level load test at the Rail Track Rocket Sled facility of the Terminal Ballistics Research Laboratory, Chandigarh.
2. The test simulated loads above the maximum flight loads.
3. It was conducted at the Satish Dhawan Space Centre, Sriharikota.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: DRDO's TBRL at Chandigarh hosted the qualification-level test on its Rail Track Rocket Sled, simulating loads above maximum flight loads. It was not at Sriharikota. Gaganyaan aims to send three astronauts to a 400 km orbit for three days on the human-rated HLVM3.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Mons Mouton, identified as a landing zone for Chandrayaan-4:
1. Chandrayaan-4 will demonstrate taking off from the lunar surface after collecting samples and bringing them to Earth.
2. Mons Mouton is a roughly 6,000 m high, largely flat-topped peak near the Moon's south pole.
3. It is named after an Indian mathematician.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Chandrayaan-4 is a sample-return mission, with a planned timeline of 2027, and its target is Mons Mouton near the south pole. The peak is named after NASA mathematician and programmer Melba Roy Mouton, not an Indian scientist.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the telescopes sanctioned in the Union Budget 2026-27:
1. The National Large Solar Telescope will be a 2-metre telescope at Merak in Ladakh.
2. A 13.7-metre segmented-mirror optical and infrared telescope will be built at Hanle.
3. The Kodaikanal Solar Observatory was established in 1975 and the Udaipur Solar Observatory in 1899.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Budget sanctioned a 2-metre solar telescope at Merak and a 13.7-metre segmented-mirror telescope at Hanle. The dates in statement 3 are reversed: Kodaikanal was established in 1899 and Udaipur in 1975. The NLST will be India's third ground-based solar observatory.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the ESA CHEOPS discovery announced in February 2026:
1. The red dwarf LHS 1903 is about 117 light-years away and hosts four planets.
2. Its outermost planet is a small rocky planet rather than a gas giant.
3. CHEOPS was launched by NASA in 2019.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: ESA's CHEOPS found that LHS 1903, 117 light-years away, has four planets with a small rocky world outermost, challenging planet-formation models. CHEOPS is an ESA mission launched on 18 December 2019, not a NASA launch.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about LIGO-India:
1. It will be located at Aundh in Hingoli district, Maharashtra.
2. It is implemented by the Department of Atomic Energy and the Department of Science and Technology with the US National Science Foundation.
3. Gravitational waves were predicted by Albert Einstein in 1905.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: LIGO-India is planned at Aundh, Hingoli, and is implemented by the DAE and DST in collaboration with the US National Science Foundation. L&T won the DAE contract to build the facility. Einstein predicted gravitational waves in 1916 from general relativity, not in 1905.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Quantum Valley project and the National Quantum Mission:
1. The foundation stone of the Quantum Valley project was laid in Amaravati, Andhra Pradesh.
2. The project seeks to install India's first 133-qubit quantum computer by 2026 with IBM, TCS and L&T.
3. The National Quantum Mission runs from 2023 to 2030-31 under the Ministry of Home Affairs.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Quantum Valley foundation stone was laid in Amaravati, with a plan for a 133-qubit computer by 2026 in a triple-helix partnership among government, industry (IBM, TCS, L&T) and academia. The National Quantum Mission, 2023 to 2030-31, is under the Ministry of Science and Technology, not Home Affairs.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs of National Quantum Mission hubs and their vertical:
1. IISc, Bengaluru : Quantum computing
2. IIT Madras : Quantum communication
3. IIT Bombay : Sensing and metrology
4. IIT Delhi : Quantum communication
How many of the above pairs are correct?
questions.e: IISc Bengaluru leads quantum computing, IIT Madras quantum communication, IIT Bombay sensing and metrology, and IIT Delhi materials and devices. IIT Delhi is not the communication hub.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about sodium-ion batteries:
1. They have a lower specific energy than lithium-ion batteries because sodium has a higher atomic mass.
2. They use aluminium current collectors on both electrodes and can be stored and transported at zero volts.
3. They show higher peak temperatures than lithium-ion cells during thermal runaway.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Sodium is heavier than lithium, so specific energy is lower, but aluminium current collectors on both electrodes let cells be stored and shipped at zero volts. Studies show lower, not higher, peak temperatures in thermal runaway, which is a safety advantage.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about India's battery manufacturing under the PLI scheme for Advanced Chemistry Cells:
1. The scheme was launched in 2021.
2. About 40 GWh of capacity has been allocated under it.
3. Nearly all of the allocated capacity has been commissioned.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The PLI scheme for Advanced Chemistry Cells began in 2021, and about 40 GWh has been allocated. Only just over 1 GWh has been commissioned so far, so deployment remains limited. India's lithium reserves are limited and not yet commercially viable.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about bio-based chemicals and enzymes:
1. Bio-based chemicals are made from biological feedstocks such as sugarcane, corn, starch or biomass residues, often through fermentation or enzymatic processes.
2. India has prioritised bio-based chemicals and enzymes under the Department of Biotechnology's BioE3 policy.
3. Enzymes generally need higher temperatures and pressures than conventional chemical catalysts, which raises energy use.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Bio-based chemicals come from biological feedstocks through fermentation or enzymes, and BioE3 lists them as a priority area. Enzymes usually work at lower temperatures and pressures than chemical catalysts, which cuts energy use and emissions.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in India:
1. The National Action Plan on AMR 2.0 covers 2025 to 2029.
2. Nafithromycin, launched in 2024, is described as India's first indigenous antibiotic.
3. The 2024 UN General Assembly meeting set a target of cutting AMR-linked deaths by 50 per cent by 2030.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: NAP-AMR 2.0 covers 2025-2029 and Nafithromycin is described as the first indigenous antibiotic. The UNGA 2024 target is a 10 per cent reduction in deaths from bacterial AMR by 2030 against the 2019 baseline, not 50 per cent. About 6 lakh lives are lost yearly in India to resistant infections.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Bacillus subtilis, declared Kerala's State microbe:
1. Kerala became the first State in the country to declare it a State microbe.
2. It is a probiotic bacterium used to produce enzymes such as amylases and proteases.
3. It is a virus found in fermented foods.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Kerala is the first State to declare Bacillus subtilis its State microbe. It is a bacterium, not a virus, found in the environment, the human gut and fermented foods, and it is used for enzymes, the antibiotic bacitracin and probiotics. Its GRAS status suits food and pharma use.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about organ donation and transplantation in India:
1. The Transplantation of Human Organs and Tissues Act, 1994 provides the legal framework.
2. NOTTO is the apex body for coordination, networking and registry of organ and tissue donation.
3. About 80 per cent of transplants now involve organs from deceased donors.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: THOTA 1994 is the legal basis and NOTTO is the apex body, with regional and State organisations below it. Around 18 per cent of transplants involve deceased donors, not 80 per cent. Transplants rose from under 5,000 in 2013 to almost 20,000 in 2025.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about India's drone regulation:
1. Nearly 90 per cent of Indian airspace has been declared a Green Zone for drone flights up to 400 feet.
2. GST on drones was reduced to 5 per cent in September 2025.
3. Civilian drone operations are permitted only for drones weighing up to 5 kg.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The liberalised Drone Rules declared nearly 90 per cent of airspace a Green Zone up to 400 feet and GST on drones was cut to 5 per cent in September 2025. Civilian operations are permitted for drones up to 500 kg, not 5 kg. Forms were cut from 25 to 5 and approvals from 72 to 4.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about drone-based government schemes:
1. The Namo Drone Didi scheme, launched in 2023, provides drones to women self-help groups for agricultural services.
2. SVAMITVA, launched in 2020, uses drone mapping of rural abadi areas to settle land disputes and improve access to bank credit.
3. SVAMITVA surveys agricultural crop fields to determine yields for crop insurance.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Namo Drone Didi supports women self-help groups with drones for spraying services, and SVAMITVA maps rural inhabited (abadi) lands to issue property cards. It does not survey crop fields for crop insurance. About 2.76 crore property cards have been issued across 31 States and Union Territories.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Kavach 4.0, in the news in February 2026:
1. Indian Railways commissioned a record 472.3 route km of it in a single day.
2. Kavach is an indigenous Automatic Train Protection system, SIL-4 certified and approved by RDSO.
3. Total Kavach 4.0 coverage of 1,306.3 route km spans fifteen railway zones.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The record 472.3 route km in one day took total Kavach 4.0 coverage to 1,306.3 route km across five railway zones, not fifteen. Kavach is SIL-4 certified and approved by RDSO and prevents signals being passed at danger and overspeeding using microprocessors, GPS and radio.
